title: What is the difference between a class and a struct in C#?
description: Understand when to use classes versus structs in C#.

data.text: **Question:** What is the difference between a class and a struct in C#?

Classes are reference types stored on the heap, while structs are value types stored on the stack. Classes support inheritance and have a default parameterless constructor, while structs cannot inherit and have an implicit parameterless constructor that initializes all fields to default values.

**Class (Reference Type):**
- Stored on the managed heap
- Variables hold a reference to the object
- Supports inheritance and polymorphism
- Can have a finalizer
- Suitable for larger objects with complex behavior
- Examples: string, arrays, custom business objects

**Struct (Value Type):**
- Stored on the stack (or inline in containing objects)
- Variables hold the actual data
- Cannot inherit from other structs or classes
- Cannot have a finalizer
- Suitable for small, immutable data structures
- Examples: int, double, DateTime, Guid

**Performance Consideration:**
- Structs avoid heap allocation and garbage collection
- But copying large structs can be expensive
- Microsoft recommends structs to be under 16 bytes

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Classes are reference types on the heap
Structs are value types on the stack
Choose based on size, mutability, and semantics
Structs should be small and immutable
data.takeaway: Use classes for most objects; reserve structs for small, immutable data.
